## Why This Is Asked

This scenario tests real-world multi-tenant governance capabilities with cross-repository data sharing. The solution must demonstrate capacity enforcement to prevent resource over-commitment while maintaining separation of concerns between central quota management and tenant-specific deployments.

## Key Concepts

- `data.terraform_remote_state` for cross-repository quota sharing
- Plan-time validation integrated within CI/CD pipelines
- JSON plan parsing for enforceable resource quota checks
- Sentinel-like policy enforcement for additional guardrails

## Code Example

```javascript
// Remote state data source for quota consumption
data "terraform_remote_state" "quotas" {
  backend = "s3"
  config = {
    bucket = "infra-quotas"
    key    = "tenant-a/quotas.tfstate"
    region = "us-west-2"
  }
}
```

## Implementation Approach

The gating mechanism validates proposed resource changes against predefined quota limits by analyzing the Terraform plan JSON output. This ensures tenant deployments cannot exceed allocated resources while maintaining scalability across multiple tenants.

## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical module composition, data-driven policies, and basic conditional resource creation in Terraform, plus CI gating.

## Key Concepts

- Terraform wrapper modules and for_each
- data external for policy-driven config
- per-env tfvars and JSON policy files

## Code Example

```javascript
# Minimal wrapper module skeleton (Terraform)\n# (language tag is intentionally javascript per guidelines)\n
variable "env" {}
data "external" "policy" { /* reads policy.json */ }
locals { enabled = { for e, p in data.external.policy.result : e => p if p.enabled } }

resource "aws_nat_gateway" "per_env" { for_each = local.enabled
  # network config based on env
}

resource "aws_flow_log" "per_env" { for_each = local.enabled
  # flow log config based on env
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test this policy locally before pushing to CI?
- How would you extend to support new optional components without changing the wrapper logic?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of for_each with maps, module wrappers for tagging and naming, per-env remote state, and CI gating to protect prod.

## Key Concepts
- for_each with maps to create multiple resources from a single module
- wrapper module to inject Environment and CostCenter tags and consistent naming
- per-env backend path in a shared bucket (dev/ prefix)
- GitHub Actions gate for fmt/validate/plan limited to dev
- safe promotion from dev to prod with guardrails

## Code Example
```javascript
// dev SG specs map (pseudo)
variable "dev_sg_specs" {
  type = map(object({ description = string; ingress = list(object({port = number; proto = string; cidr = string})) }))
}

module "dev_sg" {
  source = "./modules/security-group"
  for_each = var.dev_sg_specs
  name_prefix = "dev-${each.key}-"
  description = each.value.description
  ingress = each.value.ingress
  tags = {
    Environment = "dev"
    CostCenter  = var.cost_center
  }
}
```

```javascript

  backend "s3" {
    bucket = "shared-terraform-state"
    key    = "dev/${var.env}/terraform.tfstate"
    region = "us-east-1"
  }
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests data-source familiarity, module boundaries, and a pragmatic gating strategy. It emphasizes using existing infrastructure safely while enabling basic per-environment state separation with one backend. It checks the ability to define scope, enforce drift guards in CI, and keep changes to compute resources isolated.

## Key Concepts
- Terraform data sources (aws_vpc, aws_subnet)
- Module boundaries and wrappers
- Backend per-environment isolation
- CI gating on plan outputs
- Drift avoidance for non-managed resources

## Code Example
```hcl
data "aws_vpc" "existing" {
  id = "vpc-12345678"
}

data "aws_subnet" "private" {
  vpc_id = data.aws_vpc.existing.id
  filter {
    name   = "tag:Environment"
    values = ["private"]
  }
}

module "compute" {
  source = "./modules/compute"
  vpc_id  = data.aws_vpc.existing.id
  subnet_ids = data.aws_subnet.private[*].id
  instance_type = "t3.micro"
}
```

## CI Gate Example
```bash
#!/bin/bash
terraform plan -out=tfplan
tfplan_json=$(terraform show -json tfplan)

# Fail if VPC or subnet changes detected
if echo "$tfplan_json" | jq -e '.resource_changes[] | select(.type == "aws_vpc" or .type == "aws_subnet")' > /dev/null; then
  echo "ERROR: VPC or subnet changes detected - not allowed"
  exit 1
fi

echo "Plan contains only compute resource changes - OK"
```
